s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss with intraocular hemorrhage and crystalline deposits
salient_findings: Spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage in one eye
Presence of glistening crystals in the anterior chamber
Iridescent, needle-like crystals floating in the aqueous
key_facts: Patient is a young girl
Right eye is blind
Hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage occurred spontaneously
Multiple glistening crystals were observed in the anterior chamber
Number of aqueous crystals increased as hyphema resolved
Iridescent, needle-like crystals were seen floating in the aqueous
Morning glory optic disc anomaly was present
Low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina was observed
Chronic retinal detachment was found after vitreous hemorrhage resolution

shortlist.label: Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of iridescent, needle-like crystals in the aqueous humor

shortlist.label: Primary hyperoxaluria
shortlist.why_kept: Association with oxalate crystals in the eye

shortlist.label: Cystinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by cystine crystals in the eye

shortlist.label: Morning glory syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of morning glory optic disc anomaly

shortlist.label: Persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous
shortlist.why_kept: Association with retinal detachment and vitreous hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Coats disease
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by retinal detachment and vitreous hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Sjögren-Larsson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Association with crystalline deposits in the eye

shortlist.label: Chalcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Association with intraocular foreign body and crystalline deposits

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple, iridescent, needle-like crystals floating freely within the aqueous of the right eye is highly suggestive of cystinosis, a condition characterized by the accumulation of cystine crystals in various tissues, including the eyes.

rejected.label: Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy
rejected.why: While it involves crystalline deposits, it typically affects the cornea and retina, not the aqueous humor.

rejected.label: Primary hyperoxaluria
rejected.why: It involves oxalate crystals, not typically described as iridescent or needle-like in the aqueous humor.

rejected.label: Morning glory syndrome
rejected.why: Although a morning glory disc anomaly is present, this condition does not typically involve crystals in the aqueous humor.

rejected.label: Persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous
rejected.why: It involves abnormal development of the primary vitreous, not typically associated with iridescent crystals in the aqueous.

rejected.label: Coats disease
rejected.why: Characterized by retinal telangiectasia and exudation, not by crystals in the aqueous humor.

rejected.label: Sjögren-Larsson syndrome
rejected.why: Involves retinal changes and ichthyosis, but not typically crystals in the aqueous humor.

rejected.label: Chalcosis
rejected.why: Involves copper deposition in the eye due to an intraocular foreign body, not matching the clinical presentation of iridescent crystals in the aqueous humor.

rejected.label: Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy
rejected.why: Does not typically present with spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage or crystals in the aqueous humor as primary features.
